Mr. Speaker, I am pleased to respond to the hon. member for Vancouver-Kingsway (Mrs. Maclnnis) both courteously and, I hope, satisfactorily on this occasion although I do not expect she would be in character if she were satisfied. I question her misreading of the budget, that it helped only the elderly and students. I think the hon. member would want to include veterans also and all those Canadians who will benefit from a growing, prosperous economy.
First of all, Mr. Speaker, the combines investigation branch of the Department of Consumer and Corporate Affairs is keeping a watching brief on the situation. There has been no evidence of violations under the Combines Investigation Act, but the branch is ready and has the powers to act, indeed is required by law to act, if there are reasonable grounds for suspicion that there is a violation under the combines act. I would urge the hon. member for Vancouver-Kingsway to bring forth any evidence or indication of violations that she has, so that such action can be taken.
I believe, Mr. Speaker, that it would help to put things in perspective if we were to look at the record. As the hon. member is well aware, in late 1970 and early 1971 there was a price war among supermarket chains, particularly in eastern Canada, with a consequent severe effect on the profit of the chains. The hon. member's party might not think that profits are a significant factor, but I do not consider them evil so long as they are in line.
In the first quarter of 1972 there was a substantial increase in profits simply because they had declined so much in the previous year, and we could find no evidence of profiteering. An example might be Dominion stores which the hon. minister said had a profit increase of some 300 per cent. Their year end, I believe, is mid-March and the figures I have would indicate that their percentage of profit on sales dropped from 1.4 per cent in 1970 to .4 per cent in 1971, and then rose to 1.0 per cent in 1972 according to their recent year end statement. In 1967-68 it was 1.7 per cent, so I hardly consider this an extravagant increase in view of the fact that it was lower than before the price war. They have just recovered to the previous level. Other supermarket chains have had a similar experience. Total dollar profits have increased, there is no question about that, but sales have increased substantially-

maintopic: TRANSPORT-SUMMERSIDE P.E.I. AIR SERVICES-RESULT OF DISCUSSION WITH LOCAL REPRESENTATIVES
TRANSPORT-SUMMERSIDE P.E.I. AIR SERVICES-RESULT OF DISCUSSION WITH LOCAL REPRESENTATIVES
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, this evening I am going to deal with a question which was raised some time ago following a visit by the Minister of Transport (Mr. Jamieson) to Prince Edward Island. It was a much delayed visit, one which was planned for late last year or early this year and had a number of aspects to it, including the imminent suspension of air service to Sum-merside, P.E.I. That suspension took place in January. Prior to that we had an assurance that the minister would consult with officials in P.E.I., with the premier, with responsible officials in Summerside, with representatives of the Board of Trade and of other important groups. Unfortunately, such consultation did not take place until March.
On March 14 I asked the minister directly whether there had been consultation concerning the adequacy of air service, particularly in view of the suspension of air service to Summerside, P.E.I. I pointed out that one of the most serious aspects following the suspension was the removal of the air terminal. In light of the fact that Eastern Provincial Airlines was granted a suspension for two years, not a termination of air service, this was more than a little disquieting to the citizens who thought that a permanent decision had been taken with regard to winding up the facilities at CFB Summerside. The minister said that it was for the airline to decide about disposing of its building and facilities, but I think the minister may recognize that more is at stake than the decision taken unilaterally by Eastern Provincial Airlines.
Following the suspension of air service a number of difficulties have arisen. Some loss of time has been encountered by the business community and there has been a definite increase in air freight costs to Summerside from other parts of Canada. This I have experienced myself. There is an additional tariff involved in moving goods from Charlottetown to Summerside. In addition, it costs $10 more for a person to land at Summerside than it did prior to the air service suspension in January. This
does not please the people who live in Summerside and west of it.
Proposals have been advanced to the Canadian Transport Commission by Roberts Air Service which has indicated a willingness to provide service between Summerside and Moncton. I understand that this would be simple from the standpoint of the Canadian Transport Commission and the other competitor in the area, Eastern Provincial Airlines who operate out of Charlottetown. At the present time there may be a minor objection from EPA but not sufficient to prevent an air service to and from Summerside.
This is important for two basic reasons, Mr. Speaker. One is the importance of increased regional air service. We have seen some of this with EPA from Charlottetown to Halifax and Fredericton. Even more important is the situation with regard to Summerside because of the new lease of life given to it by the announcement of permanency. The business community and the citizens of Summer-side believe that in light of these new circumstances a more adequate air service should originate there. I hope that the representative of the Minister of Transport can tonight give us an assurance that adequate air service will be restored to Summerside.

However, I am aware of the discussions which have been held in Charlottetown on the need for air transportation in the Summerside area, in the hon. member's beautiful province where I stop when travelling to that beautiful part of my constituency located in the St. Lawrence and called the Magdalen Islands.

A number of proposals were discussed at that time, and on April 17 an application to the Canadian Transport Commission was filed by Roberts Air Service to provide service between Summerside and Moncton. Mr. Speaker, I am pleased to inform the hon. member that this matter is now before the air transport committee of the Canadian Transport Commission for consideration, and a decision is expected fairly soon.
